item.text: The financial services Royal Commission examined misconduct and behaviour that fell below community expectations in financial services businesses.
item.support:
whether any conduct of financial services entities might have amounted 
to misconduct

item.text: It considered banking, financial advice, superannuation and insurance, as well as industry culture, governance, remuneration and regulators.
item.support: The focus of this Report must be on issues, causes and responses.

item.text: The Commission concluded that rewards encouraged misconduct, customers faced unequal power and information, conflicts harmed clients’ interests and wrongdoing too often escaped proper accountability.
item.support:
the 
connection between conduct and reward; the asymmetry of power and 
information

item.text: It placed primary responsibility on the businesses concerned and their boards and senior managers.
item.support:
the primary responsibility for misconduct in 
the financial services industry lies with the entities concerned

item.text: The Commission recommended changes to lending, advice fees, insurance, superannuation, remuneration and regulatory oversight, including duties for mortgage brokers to prioritise borrowers’ interests.
item.support:
mortgage brokers must act in the best interests of 
the intending borrower.

item.quote:
Fourth, too often, financial services entities that broke the law were 
not properly held to account.

There can be no doubt that the primary responsibility for misconduct in 
the financial services industry lies with the entities concerned and those 
who managed and controlled those entities: their boards and senior 
management.
